sources.title: Diffusion Models | philippe-eecs/IDQL | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: Diffusion Models Relevant source files This document details the diffusion model implementation in IDQL (Implicit Q-Learning with Diffusion Policies). Diffusion models serve as the policy representation mechanism in this system, enabling the generation of actions from state observations through a denoising process.

sources.title: IDQL: Implicit Q-Learning as an Actor-Critic Method with Diffusion Policies
sources.snippet: Abstract Effective offline RL methods require properly handling out-of-distribution actions. Implicit Q-learning (IQL) addresses this by training a Q-function using only dataset actions through a modified Bellman backup. However, it is unclear which policy actually attains the values represented by this implicitly trained Q-function. In this paper, we reinterpret IQL as an actor-critic method ...

sources.title: Offline Training | philippe-eecs/IDQL | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: This page documents the offline training process for IDQL (Implicit Q-Learning with Diffusion Policies). Offline training refers to the methodology of training reinforcement learning agents using pre-collected datasets without direct environment interaction during the initial training phase.
